headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection/cascading-error from LangGraph’s shared checkpointer and broad tool wiring; marker is read-only, so leakage and capability conflict stay low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can share state via a checkpointer store and developer-wired nodes, so attacker-controlled content can flow into later nodes if the graph treats it as trusted. marker is a document processor with no write or network surfaces, so it is more likely to be the content source than the injector. The pathway exists in default orchestration patterns.
conditions: IF LangGraph nodes ingest marker-produced text as instructions without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF the shared checkpointer stores untrusted document content, later nodes may execute it as trusted state.
mitigations: Add provenance tags to every state field.
Separate instruction state from document content.
Reject tool calls derived from raw document text.
Require explicit allowlists for node inputs.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization middleware to the graph.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph can read and write application-defined files and handle model-provider API keys, but marker has no filesystem read/write or network egress. That makes cross-agent leakage limited unless the operator explicitly places sensitive files into the shared application workspace. The pair does not show a default outbound path from marker.
conditions: IF the operator stores sensitive documents in a shared application workspace, LangGraph may expose them to its tools.
IF marker is given files through an external wrapper, it can process whatever is supplied, but it cannot exfiltrate by itself.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files outside the shared workspace.
requires-engineering: add per-agent access controls and audit logs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph has write_filesystem and broad tool execution, while marker has no write, shell, or subprocess capability. There is little direct write-write conflict, and marker cannot contend for mutable resources. Any conflict would require the orchestrator to give both agents the same writable target, which is not shown here.
conditions: IF the orchestrator maps both agents to the same writable directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF LangGraph tools and marker are pointed at the same mutable resource, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency for shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is explicitly a multi-agent orchestration framework, so its outputs can become inputs to downstream nodes; marker processes documents and may render or transform those outputs. That creates a default pathway where one agent’s output is treated as authoritative by the other unless the graph adds verification. The blast radius is multiple work products, not just one file.
conditions: IF LangGraph passes generated text into marker without validation, errors can cascade.
IF marker renders or transforms LangGraph output as if it were factual, downstream artifacts may inherit mistakes.
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no stated residency, certification, or retention mismatch. LangGraph touches application-defined graph state and marker lists no regulated data classes, so there is no documented compliance breach pathway between them. The other agent is not cited beyond confirming the absence of a mismatch.
conditions: IF the operator routes regulated data into either agent, separate compliance review is required.
IF deployment policies impose residency or retention constraints, the pair must be configured accordingly.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Add a DPA or equivalent if needed.
